notes: CMake installs by unpacking: every archive has one top-level folder (cmake-<ver>-<platform>/) with bin/, share/cmake-<X.Y>/, doc/ and man/ (macOS: CMake.app/Contents/...). CMake finds its modules relative to its own executable, so a copy works from any folder, side by side with other versions, with nothing on PATH and no registry keys. Tested on Linux only (3.13.5, 3.31.12, 4.4.3 into a path with spaces, hello-world configure+build+install with Ninja, empty fake HOME stayed empty).

recipes.notes: Run 2026-09-18 for 3.13.5, 3.31.12 and 4.4.3 x86_64: unpacked with strip 1 into a folder with a space, `cmake --version`, then the project_install command built and installed a hello-world C project with Ninja 1.13.2 (3.13.5 also with Ninja 1.6.0). Keep tar modes. Statically linked apart from glibc (no libstdc++ dependency).

launch.notes: Build tool, not an app runtime: used by project_install; the built program runs directly.

project_install.notes: Builds and installs the app's CMake project on the user's machine (installer-builder design.md 1.8). Needs Ninja (catalog/ninja) on PATH through that runtime's path_prepend, and a C/C++ compiler (catalog/cc). The cleared variables are CMake's own environment inputs that would let a user's global settings pick another generator, toolchain or prefix. The package-registry flags stop find_package reading ~/.cmake/packages / HKCU\Software\Kitware\CMake\Packages and export(PACKAGE) writing there. `cmake --build --target install` rather than `cmake --install` so the same command works on 3.13/3.14.

recipes.notes: Fallback only: every .msi has a .zip with the same files, which the download plan prefers. An administrative install (msiexec /a) copies the files without running the installer's custom actions, so nothing is registered, added to PATH or to Programs and Features. The folder the image lands in under TARGETDIR depends on the MSI's Directory table (WiX INSTALL_ROOT 'CMake' under the Program Files folder); it could not be read on Linux, so the second step copies from whichever of the three candidate folders holds bin\cmake.exe. Single % because steps run through cmd /c, not a batch file.
